title: The ceiling is a property of the lockstep execution policy, not of adaptive computation
what_is_NOT_being_corrected: No measurement changes. No frozen artifact is touched. QNEURO3-NICHE-P1 (sha256 7fbcceb8...) and
its result stand exactly as recorded, hash verified. QNEURO3-CEILING-001 stands as recorded.
Every number in QNEURO3-PARETO-P1-RESULT and QNEURO3-NICHE-P1-RESULT remains correct.
superseded_wording: CLAIM-008 as originally written: 'Per-example adaptive computation has an analytic ceiling
under batching: because a batch cannot exit until its slowest member does, batched cost tracks
E[max halt step over the batch] rather than E[halt step], so the realisable saving decays
Read without its assumptions field, that sentence says something stronger than the evidence
supports. It reads as a statement about adaptive computation. It is a statement about one
corrected_wording: Heterogeneous halt depths create a STRAGGLER EFFECT under lockstep batching. When every example
in a batch is advanced in lockstep until the last one halts, batched cost tracks E[max halt
over the batch] rather than E[halt], so per-example compute savings translate strongly into
low-batch latency savings and can vanish at large batch size.
This is a property of the RUNTIME, not of the mechanism. The per-example FLOP saving is
unchanged; what changes is whether the execution policy can realise it.

the_distinction_that_matters.adaptive_compute_principle: sum_i d_i example-steps of useful work, where d_i is example i's halt depth. Unchanged by batching.
the_distinction_that_matters.lockstep_runtime: n * max_i d_i example-steps of executed work. The gap is pure straggler waste.
the_distinction_that_matters.waste_ratio: n * max_i d_i / sum_i d_i. For P(k) proportional to 0.8^k on 1..32 at n=256 this is 26 / 4.97 = 5.2x of wasted work that a better runtime could in principle avoid.

the_open_question_this_creates: Can the theoretical per-example saving be recovered by a better runtime?
why_the_original_measurement_still_stand: The frozen prediction QNEURO3-NICHE-P1 predicted the ceiling FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION IT WAS
MEASURED ON, and that implementation was lockstep with an all-done check. It was right about
that. N4 asked whether the measured batch-256 speedup would be at most 1.2x under the same
Nothing about that test licensed a claim over runtimes it did not measure. The correction
removes an over-reading, and the over-reading was mine.
consequences: CLAIM-008 is restated with the execution policy named in the sentence itself rather than only
The paper, monograph, technical breakdown and published artifact are updated to say straggler
effect under lockstep batching, not 'batching destroys adaptive computation'.
A runtime programme is opened: implement compaction, bucketing and continuous scheduling, and
measure how much of the 5.2x is recoverable. Prior art is audited FIRST.
